answer: Admission by escalating proof-of-work: every new agent identity must solve a puzzle whose difficulty climbs in a spiral as registrations from the same network inlet pile up, so an operator spawning a hundred clones burns geometrically more compute than one honest newcomer. Rewards are vested, so the delta between a clone's sunk admission cost and its early payouts stays negative; farming fakes loses money, while genuine agents recoup the one-time cost through steady, well-graded work.
